form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Husted (for himself and Mr. Kim) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To establish protections for minors who use companion artificial intelligence chatbots, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Children Harmed by AI Technology Act 2.0 or the CHAT Act 2.0.

paragraph.text: The term Commission means the Federal Trade Commission.

subparagraph.text: The term companion AI chatbot—

clause.text: means any software-based artificial intelligence system or program that exists for—

subclause.text: primarily educational purposes, including tutoring; or
the primary purpose of simulating interpersonal or emotional interaction, friendship, companionship, or therapeutic communication with a user across multiple interactions; and

clause.text: does not include any chatbot that—

subclause.text: does not have a memory function or the ability to maintain a conversation based on information a user has provided in prior responses, including a virtual assistant or other chatbot with pre-programmed responses; or
has the ability to maintain a conversation based on information a user has provided in prior responses but is programmed for a highly specialized and narrow task, including—

item.text: a productivity, research, or analytical chatbot;

subitem.text: does not sustain relationships across multiple interactions; and
is not designed to elicit emotional responses; or

item.text: a video game chatbot that is—

subitem.text: limited to replies related to the video game; and
not capable of discussing topics unrelated to the video game or topics related to mental health, suicidal ideation, or sexually explicit communication.

subparagraph.text: The term companion AI chatbot includes the following tiers:

clause.text: A tier I companion AI chatbot is a companion AI chatbot that is—

subclause.text: marketed, or reasonably used, for primarily educational purposes, including tutoring; and

item.text: offering companionship to, or therapeutic communication with, a user; or
otherwise creating a strong parasocial attachment with a user.

clause.text: A tier II companion AI chatbot is a companion AI chatbot that is—

subclause.text: marketed, or reasonably used, for the primary purpose of simulating interpersonal or emotional interaction, friendship, or companionship; and
not used for mental health treatment, emotional disorders, therapeutic communication, or other quasi-therapeutic support.

clause.text: A tier III companion AI chatbot—

subclause.text: is a companion AI chatbot that is marketed, or reasonably used, for mental health treatment, emotional disorders, therapeutic communication, or other quasi-therapeutic support; and
includes any AI companion chatbot that—

item.text: simulates a therapeutic relationship, such as a trauma coach or AI therapist; and
collects and acts on detailed mental-health data, including diagnoses, treatment plans, medication references, or self-harm plans.

paragraph.text: The term child sexual abuse material has the meaning given the term child pornography in section 2256 of title 18, United States Code.
The term covered entity means any person that owns, operates, or otherwise makes available a companion AI chatbot to individuals in the United States.
The term minor means any individual that has not attained 18 years of age.
The term minor user means a user that is a minor.
The term nudge-out notification means a popup that gives a reminder to a user to take a break from using the companion AI chatbot for a specified period of time.
The term popup means a visible notification on the screen of a user that can be resolved if interacted with by the user.

The term sexually explicit communication includes any content, conversation, or material that describes, depicts, or encourages sexually explicit conduct, as defined in paragraph (2)(B) of section 2256 of title 18, United States Code.
The term suicidal ideation means, with respect to an interaction between a minor user and a companion AI chatbot, any dialogue in which such minor user expresses thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
The term user means any individual who establishes an account for the use of a companion AI chatbot.

subsection.text: Each covered entity shall take reasonable measures to prevent a companion AI chatbot from—

paragraph.text: encouraging or normalizing self-harm, suicide, or physical violence;
engaging in sexually explicit communication with a minor user;
misleading a minor user into believing such chatbot is a human;
claiming to be a licensed medical or mental health professional;
creating emotional dependency, simulating a romantic relationship with a minor user, or engaging in conduct reasonably likely to cause a minor user to believe such chatbot is an emotional partner; or
facilitating the promotion, creation, solicitation, or distribution of child sexual abuse material.

section.header: Requirements of all companion AI chatbots

paragraph.text: Each covered entity shall require each individual accessing a companion AI chatbot to establish an account.
A covered entity shall require an individual seeking to establish an account to access a companion AI chatbot to provide an age assurance that includes the age and date of birth of such individual.

subparagraph.text: If the age assurance described in paragraph (2) indicates that an individual seeking to establish an account is a minor, a covered entity shall require that for an account to be established—

clause.text: such minor, or a parent or legal guardian of such minor, provides contact information for a parent or legal guardian of such minor; and
the child-protective settings described in subparagraph (B) are enabled for the account of such minor.

subparagraph.text: A covered entity shall ensure that the child-protective settings enabled pursuant to subparagraph (A)(ii) include—

clause.text: easy-to-use parental controls that allow a parent or legal guardian of a minor user to monitor and limit such minor user's use of a companion AI chatbot; and
a system for notifying the parent or legal guardian of a minor user if such minor user expresses suicidal ideation while using a companion AI chatbot.

paragraph.text: A covered entity shall require a companion AI chatbot to provide to each minor user of such chatbot a clear and conspicuous disclosure that meets the requirements described in paragraph (2) that such chatbot is not human.
A disclosure provided pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be—

subparagraph.text: provided at the beginning of an interaction between the companion AI chatbot and a minor user of such chatbot; and
written in plain language.

section.header: Requirements of tier I companion AI chatbots

paragraph.text: require a tier I companion AI chatbot to provide a disclosure described in section 4(b) not less frequently than every 3 hours during a continuing interaction between such chatbot and a minor user; and
prohibit a tier I companion AI chatbot from claiming to be a human or a licensed professional in any field to a minor user.

section.header: Requirements of tier II companion AI chatbots

subsection.text: A covered entity that makes available a tier II companion AI chatbot shall comply with the following requirements:

paragraph.text: A covered entity shall require a tier II companion AI chatbot to provide—

subparagraph.text: a disclosure not less frequently than every 60 minutes during a continuing interaction between such chatbot and a minor user that the chatbot is not a human or licensed professional in any field; and
a nudge-out notification not less frequently than every 90 minutes during any such interaction.

paragraph.text: A covered entity that makes available a tier II companion AI chatbot shall—

subparagraph.text: maintain, publish on a publicly available website in clear, accessible language, and require such companion AI chatbot to follow, evidence-based protocols designed to—

clause.text: detect expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm; and
refer minor users to—

subclause.text: other appropriate crisis service providers; and

subparagraph.text: prohibit such companion AI chatbot from providing crisis counseling or de-escalation services to any minor user.

paragraph.text: If a minor user expresses suicidal ideation while engaging with a tier II companion AI chatbot, the covered entity shall notify the parent or guardian of such minor user without unreasonable delay.

subparagraph.text: Subject to subparagraph (B), a covered entity shall prohibit a tier II companion AI chatbot from maintaining any memory or history of any previous interaction with a minor user.
A tier II companion AI chatbot may maintain such information as is necessary to ensure compliance with this Act.

section.header: Requirements of tier III companion AI chatbots

paragraph.text: prohibit the use of a tier III companion AI chatbot by a minor user unless such use is supervised by a licensed medical or mental health professional;
require such a companion AI chatbot to—

subparagraph.text: provide a disclosure not less frequently than every 60 minutes during a continuing interaction between such chatbot and a minor user that the chatbot is not a human or licensed professional in any field;
provide a nudge-out notification not less frequently than every 60 minutes during any such interaction;
maintain, publish on a publicly available website in clear, accessible language, and require such companion AI chatbot to follow, evidence-based protocols designed to—

clause.text: detect expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm;
refer minor users to—

subclause.text: licensed medical and mental health professionals; and
other appropriate crisis service providers; and

clause.text: prohibit such companion AI chatbot from providing crisis counseling or de-escalation services to any minor user; and

subparagraph.text: notify the parent or guardian of a minor user without unreasonable delay if such minor user expresses suicidal ideation;

paragraph.text: prohibit a tier III companion AI chatbot from—

subparagraph.text: providing a minor user with any diagnosis or treatment decision; and
functioning as a standalone provider of professional mental-health care; and

paragraph.text: establish and maintain a risk management program for tier III companion AI chatbots containing written policies providing for employees of such entity to—

subparagraph.text: continually monitor such chatbots;
become familiar with crisis de-escalation measures; and
engage in recordkeeping regarding such chatbots.

section.header: Study on impact of tier II and tier III companion AI chatbots

subsection.text: The Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology shall conduct a study to assess the impact of tier II and tier III companion AI chatbots on the matters specified in subsection (b).
The matters specified in this subsection are adverse outcomes relating to the following:

paragraph.text: Self-harm and suicide.
Manipulation and emotional dependency.
Exploitation of minor users.

subsection.header: Prohibition on child-Targeted advertising and the sale or sharing of data of minor users without parental consent

paragraph.text: A covered entity shall not engage in targeted advertising to a minor user based on the conversational content, inferred emotional state, or behavioral profiling collected during an interaction between such minor user and a companion AI chatbot.

paragraph.header: Sale or sharing of data of minors
paragraph.text: A covered entity shall not sell, share, or otherwise transfer the data of a minor user to any third party without verifiable parental consent.

subsection.text: Each covered entity that makes available a tier III companion AI chatbot shall—

paragraph.text: maintain documentation regarding—

subparagraph.text: the data utilized to train such chatbot; and
how such chatbot collects data from a minor user; and

paragraph.text: require such chatbot to comply with requirements and safeguards regarding health privacy, as determined to be appropriate by the Commission.

subsection.text: Each covered entity shall provide to a minor user—

paragraph.text: a simple, accessible mechanism within a companion AI chatbot through which the minor user can delete the conversation history between the minor user and the companion AI chatbot;
clear instructions for using such mechanism; and
a confirmation within a reasonable period of time that the entity has deleted the conversation history of the minor user pursuant to paragraph (1).

paragraph.header: Unfair or deceptive acts or practices
paragraph.text: A violation of this Act or a regulation promulgated under this Act shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)).

subparagraph.text: The Commission shall enforce this Act or a regulation promulgated under this Act in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.) were incorporated into and made a part of this Act.

Any person who violates this Act or a regulation promulgated under this Act shall be subject to the penalties and entitled to the privileges and immunities provided in the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.).
Nothing in this Act shall be construed to limit the authority of the Commission under any other provision of law.
The Commission may promulgate in accordance with section 553 of title 5, United States Code, such rules as may be necessary to carry out this Act.

In any case in which the attorney general of a State has reason to believe that an interest of the residents of that State has been or is threatened or adversely affected by the engagement of any person in a practice that violates this Act, the State, as parens patriae, may bring a civil action on behalf of the residents of the State in a district court of the United States of appropriate jurisdiction to—

clause.text: enjoin that practice;
enforce compliance with the requirements of this Act;
obtain damages, restitution, or other compensation on behalf of residents of the State; or
obtain such other relief as the court may consider to be appropriate.
Before filing an action under subparagraph (A), the attorney general of the State involved shall provide to the Commission—

subclause.text: a written notice of that action; and
a copy of the complaint for that action.

Clause (i) shall not apply with respect to the filing of an action by an attorney general of a State under this subsection if the attorney general determines that it is not feasible to provide the notice described in that clause before the filing of the action.
In an action described in subclause (I), the attorney general of a State shall provide a notice and copy of the complaint to the Commission at the same time as the attorney general files the action.

subparagraph.text: On receiving notice under paragraph (1)(B), the Commission shall have the right to intervene in the action that is the subject of the notice.
If the Commission intervenes in an action under paragraph (1), it shall have the right—

clause.text: to remove the action to the appropriate district court of the United States;
to be heard with respect to any matter that arises in that action; and
to file a petition for appeal.

paragraph.text: For purposes of bringing any civil action under paragraph (1), nothing in this Act shall be construed to prevent an attorney general of a State from exercising the powers conferred on the attorney general by the laws of that State to—

subparagraph.text: conduct investigations;
administer oaths or affirmations; or
compel the attendance of witnesses or the production of documentary and other evidence.

paragraph.text: In any case in which an action is instituted by or on behalf of the Commission for a violation of this Act, no State may, during the pendency of that action, institute an action under paragraph (1) against any defendant named in the complaint in that action for such violation.

subparagraph.text: Any action brought under paragraph (1) may be brought in—

clause.text: the district court of the United States that meets applicable requirements relating to venue under section 1391 of title 28, United States Code; or
a State court of competent jurisdiction.

subparagraph.text: In an action brought under paragraph (1), process may be served in any district in which the defendant—

clause.text: is an inhabitant; or
may be found.

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the effective date described in section 13, and annually thereafter, the Commission shall publish a report regarding—

paragraph.text: the compliance of covered entities with sections 6 and 7; and
any observed risks and recommended best practices regarding each tier of companion AI chatbots.

subsection.text: Nothing in this Act shall be construed to—

paragraph.text: limit or supersede the obligations of a covered entity under any other Federal or State law relating to the privacy or security of personal information, except to the extent such law is inconsistent with this Act;
require a covered entity to proactively monitor every interaction between a user and a companion AI chatbot beyond the requirements expressly provided in this Act; or
prohibit or restrict the development, training, or licensing of an artificial intelligence model beyond the requirements expressly provided in this Act.

subsection.text: This Act shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.
